title: Write a letter to your future self
description: A short letter, sealed away for six months or a year, is a kind conversation with the person you are becoming.

body.heading: What to put in it
paragraphs: Write as you would to a good friend. Say what life looks like right now: what you are working on, what is worrying you, what is making you laugh. Details that feel ordinary today will be fascinating later.
Add a few honest hopes, not demands. 'I hope you are still drawing' lands more kindly than a list of achievements your future self must report back on.

body.heading: Seal it and set the date
paragraphs: Put the letter in an envelope, write the opening date on it, and store it somewhere safe: a drawer, a box, or with a trusted person. Some people use an email service that delivers later; a paper letter works just as well.
When the day comes, read it slowly. Notice what changed, what stayed, and what your past self got right about you. Then, if you like, write the next one.

takeaway: Tell your future self what life is like now, kindly and in detail.
